title: Precise synthesis of targeted noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials.

recollection.starting_material: Aqueous solutions of noble metal precursors (e.g. H2PtCl6, Pd(NO3)2, AuCl3, AgNO3, and RhCl3)
recollection.intervention: Sequential and simultaneous reduction in a microemulsion template under inert atmosphere with controlled pH and temperature (∼80 °C) using NaBH4 as a reducing agent
recollection.structure: Monodisperse 2–5 nm single‐phase face‐centered‐cubic nanoparticles with uniform elemental distribution at the atomic scale
recollection.mechanism: Entropy‐driven alloying facilitated by rapid nucleation in confined micellar domains, followed by slow growth that ensures homogenous mixing; lattice strain and surface segregation minimized by high configurational entropy
recollection.results: Yield of >90% HEA nanoparticles; atomic‐level composition deviation <5 at.%; specific activity for oxygen reduction reaction of ∼1.2 mA cm−2 at 0.9 V (vs. RHE), up to 3× higher than commercial Pt/C; durable over 10 000 cycles with <10% loss in activity

score.note: The recollection describes an unrelated microemulsion/NaBH4 nanoparticle synthesis. The actual work used spray drying followed by H2 thermal decomposition-reduction to form porous 3D nanoframeworks with composition-dependent fcc/hcp structures. Its proposed noble-metal-assisted hydrogen reduction and Pt–Ru phase-transition mechanisms are absent, and all reported performance metrics and reaction targets differ from the paper.
